keep: The idea is named up front in plain words: switches kept fully on or off, on-time varied so the average traces a sine, the winding's inductance smoothing the current to follow it.

The picture is the brief's sine from pulses: a 540 V link, a picker for One leg, H-bridge and Three legs, a sine reference against a triangle carrier, the pulses with their dashed local average, the motor current as a near-sine with a sawtooth, sliders for depth, reference frequency, carrier frequency and dead time, red shoot-through at zero dead time, a flattened sine when it is long, and the UPS, drive and shore converter card on the last screen.

The cause is drawn and taught from lesson 6's rule: a leg's average is D x 540 V, D = 50% + 50% x depth x the reference, the mirror leg gives (2D - 1) x 540 V, and three legs 120 degrees apart give sqrt3 x 270 V peak between lines, 331 V rms at full depth. Every result is computed on the screen from those rules.
The brief's recall opener (Motors: 200 V at 25 Hz from a 400 V, 50 Hz motor) is screen 1, and screen 11 answers it from the fixed 540 V link: 25 Hz reference, 60% depth, 198 V.

Misconceptions each get a DO screen with their own hints: a zero on the reference read as the switch off (5), the winding seeing one leg's average (7), the carrier setting the output frequency (9), changing the link or the carrier to change the output (11), longer dead time read as only safer (13), and a UPS changing over on mains failure (14).

The lesson cites eight sources, footnotes kept to rules and values he might look up.
Fourteen screens: a recall opener, SHOW 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 each followed by a DO, ending with two mixed puzzles. Every SHOW is under 90 words (67 to 83).
